Headquarters: Remote
 
URL: https://retr.app/

About RETR

RETR is a mortgage market intelligence platform. Loan officers use us to find the real estate agents worth building relationships with, mortgage companies use us to recruit top producers, and lenders use us to decide who to lend their money through. More than 55% of the Top 100 mortgage lenders are customers.

We were founded in 2022, we are bootstrapped and profitable, and we have never taken outside money. We grew because loan officers told other loan officers about us. That word of mouth is the whole company in one sentence, and it is why customer outcomes are not a service function here. They are the growth engine.

We are fully remote and we operate on a few principles: lead with value, do the right thing, be generous without keeping score. We hire for honesty, integrity, fairness, accountability, and excellence, and we have very little appetite for process that does not earn its place.

The role

This is one of the first Customer Success Managers at RETR, and you will own a book of our enterprise customers end to end: the relationships, the value they get, the renewal, and the growth.

Our enterprise customers are held today by the founders, sales, support, and enablement, and they are held well. This role exists because the book has outgrown what any of them can carry alongside their own jobs. You get a defined set of accounts and the time to go deep on them: exactly how each one is doing, what it needs next, and where it should be a year from now.

You will report to our VP of Customer Advocacy and work alongside the account executives who own new business and large expansions, and the trainers who run onboarding and group sessions.

What you own

Four things. Everything else you do should move one of them.

A plan for every customer. A short written plan for every account in your book: why they bought, who the people are, what they are trying to accomplish, how they actually use the product, where the risk is, and what happens next. New accounts get one within 30 days. Plans get refreshed before every review and every renewal.

The renewal. You own the path to renewal from the day the account joins your book, not from 30 days out. Risk gets named early, in writing, with a plan against it. Nothing should churn without someone having seen it coming.

Expansion. Growth comes from value: new use cases, new features, new product lines, new teams and branches, and the seats that follow once people see what it is worth. You run the smaller expansions yourself and bring in an account executive on the larger ones. Part of your pay is tied to this, and it should feel like the natural result of doing the rest of the job well.

Advocates. Healthy customers become references, case studies, testimonials, referrals, and beta participants. In an industry this relationship-driven, a customer willing to vouch for us is worth more than most marketing we could buy.

Underneath those four, the work is: knowing how customers use RETR and helping them use it better, building relationships with executive sponsors and daily users alike, reading health from adoption and conversation rather than guessing, and bringing what you hear back into the company so the product and the experience get better.

What this role is not

It is not reactive account management, and it is not a job you win by holding a set number of calls a week. Calls matter, but what matters is what happens on them: the relationship built, the plan moved, the value shown, the joy created.

It is not a support queue. We have a support team and they are good. You are not the escalation path for every ticket in your book.

Because we are still building the Customer Advocacy function, you won't be stepping into a perfectly defined playbook. You'll help create it. We want someone who is energized by that.

How we work

RETR is intentionally lean. Automation before hiring, systems before managers, one to many before one to one. Technology and AI should absorb the work that does not need human judgment, so our people spend their time where people are worth the most: understanding a customer's business, solving a real problem, building a relationship, finding the opportunity nobody else saw.

So we do not want CSMs living in spreadsheets or doing repetitive admin. We want them thinking, and immersed/obsessed with our customers.

We are fully remote and async first. We write things down. We measure what you deliver, and in this role that is the health of your book.

What success looks like

A great CSM here can answer these about any account, at any moment, without opening a file:

• Why did this customer buy RETR?

• How are they using it today, and who actually uses it?

• Are they getting value, and how do we know?

• Who inside the organization cares, and who signs the renewal?

• Where could we create more value for them?

• What could cost us this renewal?

• What happens next, and when?

In your first 30 days you will know your book: the renewals coming, the accounts at risk, and the people who matter in each. By 60 days every account has a plan and you have met the sponsors who count. By 90 days you are running the full scorecard, with your first expansions in motion.

Over a year, the work shows up as deeper adoption, earlier risk detection, stronger retention and expansion, and a list of customers willing to say so publicly. Most of all, our customers should feel that RETR understands their business and is invested in it.

What we're looking for

You are probably a strong fit if you:

• Have 3+ years in customer success, account management, or another customer-facing SaaS role, owning a book with renewal or expansion targets.

• Get genuinely curious about how a customer's business makes money, and can connect our product to the outcomes they care about.

• Are comfortable owning the commercial health of an account, not just the relationship: the renewal, the risk, the growth.

• Spot expansion that comes from real value, without turning every conversation into a pitch.

• Notice problems early and act before anyone asks you to.

• Move fast. Customers hear back from you quickly, and plans turn into action in days, not weeks.

• Build relationships deep enough that customers want to vouch for you.

• Use data, AI, and automation to decide where to focus, and save your own time for the conversations that need a person.

• Communicate clearly with everyone from a daily user to a C-level executive.

• Like building playbooks and doing well when the answer is not written down yet.

• Are motivated by having part of your pay tied to keeping and growing your customers.

• Work well with the account executives, support, and enablement people who share your accounts, and make them better at their jobs. 

• Get real energy out of a customer who is winning, and are not satisfied until they are.

Mortgage experience is a major plus. If you have worked in or sold into mortgage lending, whether at a lender, a broker, a vendor, a title or settlement company, or anywhere else in the ecosystem, say so clearly in your application. Our customers are loan officers, branch managers, and mortgage executives whose income moves with rates. Someone who already understands mortgage origination, recruiting, relationship building, and how a loan officer actually spends their day, starts contributing months earlier and earns credibility in the room on the first call.

It is a strong preference, not a requirement. Adjacent fintech, real estate, or proptech experience counts for a lot too, and we will take how you think and operate over a resume line every time.

Compensation and benefits

Base salary $85,000. On-target earnings $115,000, including $30,000 of variable at 100% of target, paid quarterly. Variable can reach 150% of target for strong performance, which puts total earnings around $130,000. Base is a national figure with no location adjustment.

1a887cb9e59ee2fd.description: **About Metaforms** At Metaforms, we're redefining how market research gets done. Market research still runs on legacy survey platforms, manual project operations, fragmented handoffs, and domain expertise locked in a few specialists' heads. Metaforms is building the agent layer that makes this work dramatically more efficient — without lowering the bar for quality, accuracy, or client trust. Our vertically integrated AI platform empowers agencies like Dynata, Savanta, and Borderless Access to scale 10x faster, with AI Agents augmenting survey programming, data processing, and project management. We process 1,000+ surveys monthly, serve agencies working with Fortune 500 companies, and are backed by $9M in Series A funding to aggressively scale. The product surface here is unusual. Surveys behave like programs, business workflows contain hidden operational nuance, and a small mistake creates real downstream cost for an agency and its clients. Product thinking at Metaforms isn't about copying familiar SaaS patterns — it's about understanding how work actually gets done, identifying where AI agents can reliably help, and shaping systems that feel intuitive to users while introducing genuinely new workflows underneath. **The Role** We're hiring a Product Manager to define and ship new AI-native products and workflow experiences for research operations. The role sits at the intersection of user discovery, domain synthesis, product design, and engineering execution. You'll go end to end — from interviewing users and subject matter experts, to identifying operational bottlenecks, to translating business needs into concrete requirements, to partnering closely with engineering through delivery. This is a high-ownership role for someone who thrives in ambiguous spaces, reasons from first principles, and builds from zero rather than relying on existing category templates. **What You'll Own** *User Discovery & Problem Definition* - Conduct frequent interviews with research operators, project managers, survey programmers, and agency leaders to understand how work actually happens - Turn messy qualitative input into clear product insights, problem statements, and opportunity areas - Work closely with subject matter experts to separate surface requests from deeper workflow and systems problems - Build conviction on where AI agents can remove manual effort, improve turnaround, or raise quality — without disrupting critical trust points *Product Design & 0→1 Development* - Define new product concepts, workflow patterns, and operating models for AI-assisted research work - Design familiar-feeling user journeys that introduce new capabilities without overwhelming users - Write requirements specific enough for engineering to execute, while preserving room for iteration where the solution space is still emerging - Iterate rapidly on prototypes, internal feedback, and early customer usage to converge on products that are both useful and operationally viable *Cross-Functional Execution* - Translate business requirements into clear engineering asks — scope, constraints, acceptance criteria, and edge cases - Partner tightly with engineering, design, operations, and domain experts through the build cycle - Drive prioritization by balancing customer value, technical feasibility, reliability risk, and speed - Ensure the team is solving the right problem, not just shipping the fastest version of the first idea *Product Quality & Adoption* - Define what "good" looks like for product outcomes, user trust, and workflow adoption - Identify failure modes in user flows, handoffs, and agent behavior — especially in high-consequence operational steps - Close the loop between shipped behavior, customer feedback, and roadmap decisions - Own rollout, onboarding, and change management with customer success and operators so new workflows land in real agency production — including how adoption and efficiency gains are measured **Representative Problems You Might Work On** - Designing an AI-assisted workflow that turns a raw client questionnaire into an executable survey build process - Creating review and approval loops where human operators guide or validate agent output without adding unnecessary friction - Reworking a fragmented project-management flow into a single experience that makes bottlenecks, state, and exceptions visible - Defining how internal subject matter experts collaborate with product and engineering to encode operational knowledge into a scalable system - Building product surfaces that feel familiar to agency teams while delivering step-change improvements in speed and efficiency **What We're Looking For** *Must-have* - Proven product management experience shipping software from concept to launch - Demonstrated ability to operate in ambiguous, early-stage, or zero-to-one environments - Strong user discovery skills — interviewing, pattern extraction, and synthesis into product direction - Comfort going deep with subject matter experts and operational stakeholders in initially unfamiliar domains - What You'll Do

We are looking for experienced Machine Learning Engineers with a background in software development

and a deep enthusiasm for solving complex problems. You will lead a dynamic team dedicated to designing

and implementing a large language model framework to power diverse applications across Avalara. Your

responsibilities will span the entire development lifecycle, including conceptualization, prototyping and

delivery of the LLM platform features.

You will have a blend of technical skills in the fields of AI & Machine Learning especially with LLMs and a

deep-seated understanding of software development practices where you'll work with a team to ensure

our systems are scalable, performant and accurate. You will be reporting to Senior Manager, AI/ML.

This is a role.

What Your Responsibilities Will Be

We are looking for engineers who can think quick and have a background in implementation. Your

Responsibilities Will Include

• Build on top of the foundational framework for supporting Large Language Model Applications at Avalara
• Experience with LLMs - like GPT, Claude, LLama and other Bedrock models
• Leverage best practices in software development, including Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) along with appropriate functional and unit testing in place.
• Inspire creativity by researching and applying the latest technologies and methodologies in machine learning and software development.
• Write, review, and maintain high-quality code that meets industry standards.
• Lead code review sessions, ensuring good code quality and documentation.
• Mentor junior engineers, encouraging a culture of collaboration.
• Proficiency in developing and debugging software with a preference for Python, though familiarity with additional programming languages is valued and encouraged.

What You’ll Need To Be Successful

Bachelor's/master’s degree in computer science with 5+ years of industry experience in software

development, along with experience building Machine Learning models and deploying them in

production environments.

• Proficiency working in cloud computing environments (AWS, Azure, GCP), Machine Learning frameworks, and software development best practices.
• Work with technological innovations in AI & ML(esp. GenAI)
• Experience with design patterns and data structures.
• Good analytical, design and debugging skills.

Technologies You Will Work With

Python, LLMs, MLFlow, Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, AWS, GitLab, Postgres, Prometheus, Grafana

Avalara is an AI-first Company

AI is embedded in our workflows, decision-making, and products. Success here requires embracing AI as an essential capability.

• You’ll bring experience using AI and AI-related technologies, ready to thrive here.
• You’ll apply AI every day to business challenges - improving efficiency, contributing solutions, and driving results for your team, our company, and our customers.
• You’ll grow with AI by staying curious about new trends and best practices, and by sharing what you learn so others can benefit too.

How We’ll Take Care Of You

Total Rewards

In addition to a great compensation package, paid time off, and paid parental leave, many Avalara employees are eligible for bonuses.

Health & Wellness

Benefits vary by location but generally include private medical, life, and disability insurance.

Inclusive culture and diversity

Avalara strongly supports diversity, equity, and inclusion, and is committed to integrating them into our business practices and our organizational culture. We also have a total of 8 employee-run resource groups, each with senior leadership and exec sponsorship.

What You Need To Know About Avalara

We’re defining the relationship between tax and tech.

We’ve already built an industry-leading cloud compliance platform, processing over 54 billion customer API calls and over 6.6 million tax returns a year. Our growth is real - we're a billion dollar business - and we’re not slowing down until we’ve achieved our mission - to be part of every transaction in the world.

We’re bright, innovative, and disruptive, like the orange we love to wear. It captures our quirky spirit and optimistic mindset. It shows off the culture we’ve designed, that empowers our people to win. We’ve been different from day one. Join us, and your career will be too.

We’re An Equal Opportunity Employer

Supporting diversity and inclusion is a cornerstone of our company — we don’t want people to fit into our culture, but to enrich it. All qualified candidates will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, creed, religion, age, gender, national orientation, disability, sexual orientation, US Veteran status, or any other factor protected by law. If you require any reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process, please let us know.
